notes: Dialogue kept word for word; the opening narration is dropped because the church and his first line show the confession. The man is old (he hid someone in WWII), so grandpa plays him in a flat cap; the hidden man is only mentioned.
title: Die Beichte

lines.text: Vergib mir Vater, ich habe gesündigt.
Was hast du getan, mein Sohn?
Im Zweiten Weltkrieg habe ich einen Juden auf meinem Dachboden versteckt.
Aber das ist doch keine Sünde.
Ich sagte zu ihm, dass er für zwanzig Gulden die Woche so lange bleiben kann, wie er will.
Da hast du doch etwas Gutes getan.
Danke, das erleichtert mich sehr. Eine Frage hätte ich aber noch.
Ja, mein Sohn?
Soll ich ihm sagen, dass der Krieg vorbei ist?

notes: Translated line by line; Gulden replaced with dollars as asked. Opening narration dropped, the church and the first line show the confession. Grandpa in a flat cap plays the old man; the hidden man is only mentioned.
title: Исповедь

lines.text: Простите меня, святой отец, я согрешил.
Что ты сделал, сын мой?
Во время Второй мировой войны я прятал еврея у себя на чердаке.
Но это же не грех.
Я сказал ему, что за двадцать долларов в неделю он может оставаться там сколько захочет.
Так ты же сделал доброе дело.
Спасибо, у меня прямо камень с души. Но у меня есть ещё один вопрос.
Да, сын мой?
Мне сказать ему, что война закончилась?

notes: Translated line by line; Gulden replaced with dollars as asked. Opening narration dropped, the church and the first line show the confession. Grandpa in a flat cap plays the old man; the hidden man is only mentioned.
title: Confession

lines.text: Forgive me, Father, for I have sinned.
What have you done, my son?
During the Second World War I hid a Jewish man in my attic.
But that's no sin.
I told him that for twenty dollars a week he could stay as long as he liked.
Well, you did a good thing.
Thank you, that's a great relief. But I do have one more question.
Yes, my son?
Should I tell him the war is over?

notes: Wording kept; the wife's and the psychiatrist's speeches split into short lines. Narrator keeps the source sentence because the joke needs him to be a psychiatrist. The husband is only mentioned.
title: Das Beste an einer Tasse

lines.text: Eine Frau geht zum Psychiater, um sich über ihren Mann zu beschweren.
Mein Mann ist total bekloppt.
Zum Frühstück trinkt er den Kaffee aus und isst dann die Kaffeetasse mit.
Nur den Henkel lässt er übrig.
Ja, das ist schon verrückt.
Der Henkel ist doch das Beste an der Tasse.

notes: Translated line by line; the narrator keeps the source sentence because the joke needs him to be a psychiatrist. The husband is only mentioned.
title: Самое лучшее в чашке

lines.text: Женщина приходит к психиатру пожаловаться на мужа.
Мой муж совсем чокнутый.
На завтрак он выпивает кофе, а потом съедает и саму чашку.
Оставляет только ручку.
Да, это действительно ненормально.
Ручка ведь самое лучшее в чашке.

notes: Translated line by line; the narrator keeps the source sentence because the joke needs him to be a psychiatrist. The husband is only mentioned.
title: The Best Part of the Cup

lines.text: A woman goes to a psychiatrist to complain about her husband.
My husband is totally nuts.
At breakfast he drinks up his coffee and then eats the coffee cup too.
He only leaves the handle.
Yes, that really is crazy.
The handle is the best part of the cup.

notes: Dialogue kept word for word; fixed the typo 'meine Sohn'. The joke needs the mother to pass for a man, so zhena gets short hair and dull clothes; the homely boy sits on screen, silent. Bus variant with a few passengers.
title: Konversation im Bus

lines.text: Boah, ist der Junge da drüben grässlich.
Hey, das ist mein Sohn.
Oh Entschuldigung, ich wusste nicht, dass Sie der Vater sind.
Hey!! Ich bin seine Mutter!

notes: Translated line by line. The joke needs the mother to pass for a man, so zhena gets short hair and dull clothes; the homely boy sits on screen, silent. Bus variant with a few passengers.
title: Разговор в автобусе

lines.text: Ох, ну и страшный же вон тот мальчишка.
Эй, это мой сын.
Ой, извините, я не знал, что вы его отец.
Эй!! Я его мать!

notes: Translated line by line. The joke needs the mother to pass for a man, so zhena gets short hair and dull clothes; the homely boy sits on screen, silent. Bus variant with a few passengers.
title: Bus Conversation

lines.text: Wow, that boy over there is hideous.
Hey, that's my son.
Oh, sorry, I didn't know you were his father.
Hey!! I'm his mother!

notes: Reported dialogue turned into direct lines, words kept; 'Arsch' stays because the punchline turns it into an insult for the husband. Narrator keeps the source opening, since the couple's age matters. The boss is only mentioned.
title: Das Kompliment

lines.text: Ein nicht mehr ganz junges Ehepaar sitzt beim Abendessen.
Mein Chef hat mir heute ein Kompliment für mein schönes Dekolleté gemacht!
Und zu deinem schlaffen Arsch hat er nichts gesagt?
Nein, über dich haben wir gar nicht gesprochen!

notes: Translated line by line. 'Arsch' is 'задница' in the clean text and 'жопа' in uncensored; both also work as an insult for a person, so the punchline survives. The boss is only mentioned.
title: Комплимент

lines.text: Немолодая супружеская пара ужинает.
Мой начальник сегодня сделал мне комплимент за моё красивое декольте!
А про твою дряблую задницу он ничего не сказал?
lines.uncensored: А про твою дряблую жопу он ничего не сказал?

lines.text: Нет, о тебе мы вообще не говорили!

notes: Translated line by line; 'ass' works both as body part and as an insult, so the punchline lands as in German. The boss is only mentioned.
title: The Compliment

lines.text: A not-so-young married couple is having dinner.
My boss complimented me on my lovely cleavage today!
And he didn't say anything about your saggy ass?
No, we didn't talk about you at all!
